observation.problem: Post-semantic-freeze note-main SHA churn from concurrent independent workers was being treated as a universal hard semantic stop even when a role's relevant authoritative control/config blob identities were unchanged.
observation.inference: With many scheduled workers persisting role-local artifacts and receipts to one main branch, an any-main-SHA post-freeze stop creates mutual starvation and lowers useful-output rate without adding control-integrity protection when relevant identities are byte-identical.

change.rule: Keep strict H1/H2 bootstrap and freeze the approved authoritative identity set at first semantic read. After freeze, unrelated main movement alone is not a stop. Later-head visibility may only verify exact authoritative blob identity; newer-head semantic content remains forbidden. Stop/defer on any changed or unverifiable relevant identity or own-state/input CAS conflict.

rollback.condition: If a revision21 execution consumes newer-head semantics, misses a real authoritative root/role/downstream config change, crosses CLEAN isolation, or continues after authoritative identity cannot be verified, increment root control and restore the stricter revision20 post-freeze stop semantics.

exact_next_action: Validate the first revision21 evaluation and downstream executions against both unchanged-identity unrelated head drift and genuine/unverifiable relevant-control drift. Require evaluation checker-v2 durable precommit before first execution and the duplicate negative, low-usefulness negative and matched positive controls; then require evidence_comparator config13 independent recomputation. Preserve the 14-role denominator; do not change novelty platform enablement without explicit user authorization.
